# Mission 33 — teacher notes (Final project: one change, tested and measured with confidence)

Teacher only. Rebuilt 2026-10-15 on NAVERA Lite. **Students never see or touch NAVERA's code**: the project is ONE
change to their own complete NAVERA Lite (`~/lessons/33-final-project/navera_lite/`, every part finished, the whole
reference suite), proved with a pre-registration, a red test, two campaigns of the headless simulator flown from git
commits, a paired bootstrap interval and a report.

**What the students get.** The whole stack (manifest `"*"`, generated by `tools/lite_build.py`, no TODO in any part) and
its 22 test files (164 tests, all pass in the sandbox, ≈ 13 s; outside it `test_tiles` skips one without the map); `navera_lite/tools/init_repo.sh` (mission 14);
**new given part** `navera_lite/tools/adopt.py` (`# @part 33`): replaces the course's parts by the student's own,
taken from the earlier lesson folders (the ✏️ rows of their `PARTS.md`; the latest mission wins), each only if it has
no TODO left, defines every public name of the course's version and passes its own course test; `--apply` also needs
the whole suite and one flight to pass, else changes nothing; writes `navera_lite/MINE.md`. Its gate is only as strong as
the course's tests: a student `geo.py` with a 1 % wrong Earth radius passes `test_geo.py` (tested 2026-10-15) and
is adopted — then the student's campaigns fly their own (slightly wrong) stack, which is the point; MINE.md tells you
which parts are theirs. Mission files
(hand-written): `project.py` (the bench, frozen: plan / red / campaign before|after / green / evaluate / status / one /
metrics), `project.json` (template with `_help` lines), `REPORT.md` (8 fixed sections), `answers.py`, `my_metric.py`
(only for a custom metric), `campaign/*.json` (31's scenarios + `lake.json` + `night_lag.json`), `ref_desc.pt` and
`ref_homography.pt` (31's weights: the stack's networks, the file idea 9 retrains), `runner_kit.py`, `academy_gpu.py`,
`pytest.ini`. No dataset: the simulator's corridor is mission 31's (`/data/academy/31-simulator`, read by
`sim/run.py`). The old `datasets/33-final-project/` (NMEA bench, its truth and its generator — public!) was deleted.

**What changed from the old mission 33.** The old project branched and patched the NAVERA copy (a GPS driver example and
ten NAVERA ideas with NAVERA paths). All gone. The method stays (proposal first, failing test, paired block/iid
bootstrap, accept/reject/inconclusive, patch), the object is the student's own stack, the data are their own campaigns.
The statistics tools are no longer re-written (mission 32's `stats.py` is used). The "garden of forking paths" idiom
is named with its source (Gelman and Loken 2013) and explained.

## How the bench works (what to tell a puzzled student)

- `project.py campaign before|after` runs `git archive <sha>` of the tag `before` / of `HEAD` into
  `runs/.code/<sha12>/` and flies, in ONE Python process, every scenario of `project.json` × the block of seeds with
  that commit's `navera_lite` (`sim.run.fly` + `sim.run.write`, `--mine` never: the stack of the folder IS theirs).
  `runs/<label>/manifest.json` records the sha, the hash of project.json, the runs and a sha256 per CSV.
  `runs/.gitignore` (`*`) keeps runs out of git. "after" refuses a dirty stack or a project.json that differs from
  the baseline's.
- `evaluate`: per-run metric (window "fault" = first fault → that sensor back to "ok" or the end; "all"; [t0, t1]),
  statistic mean (or |mean − target| for "closer"), D = stat(after) − stat(before), `stats.paired_diff_ci` (iid over
  runs, B 2000, seed `boot_seed`), guard-rail the same with seed + 1, Wilson per side for 0/1 metrics, decision:
  accept = whole CI beyond `min_effect` on the good side AND guard-rail's worst plausible loss ≤ `max_loss`; reject =
  whole CI on the bad side of 0 OR guard-rail's smallest plausible loss > `max_loss`; else inconclusive.
- Iid bootstrap over runs is honest (independent seeds); this is the lesson's contrast with mission 32's seconds.
- **Round 1 additions (2026-10-15).** `project.json` holds the **hypothesis** (required, ≥ 6 words); the directions
  are fixed by each metric (`METRICS[...][3]`: errors lower, availability/fix_share/detected higher, honest2 closer;
  a guard-rail cannot be "closer"); a metric or the guard-rail may hold `"scenarios": [...]` (a subset of the
  campaign's files: ideas 2, 7, 8 put the metric on a fault scenario and the guard-rail on an honest one);
  `campaign before` refuses at once a metric undefined in some baseline run; a **0/1 metric or guard-rail** gets an
  interval never narrower than Newcombe's hybrid score interval from two Wilson intervals (the unpaired form, Newcombe
  1998 method 10: conservative for positively correlated pairs; used only as a floor) (0/30 vs 0/30 → about
  [−0.114, 0.114], not [0, 0]); every 'after' campaign and evaluation goes into `runs/journal.txt`, `evaluate` warns
  when more than one after-commit was evaluated against a baseline, and check 10 then requires section 8 to name
  each commit id; the template's seeds start at 1001 (explore below 1000). For "closer" the interval of
  |mean − target| is conservative when the after-mean is within about one standard error of the target.
- **The seal (server).** When check 5 first passes, the check reports `seal = <before sha12>:<sha256(project.json)[:12]>`;
  the server (`server/seals.py`, `state/seals.json`) keeps the FIRST value per student and mission and hands it to
  every later check; check 3 fails if `before` or its project.json moved after the Pre-registered badge. To allow a
  new pre-registration: `python3 tools/seal.py reset <student> 33-final-project` (list: `tools/seal.py list`);
  deleting the student, or `tools/try_lesson.py` reinstalling the lesson, resets it. No dashboard button yet.

## What check.py verifies (12 checks) — and what it cannot

| # | Check | How |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | repo + tag start + project.py unchanged | `.git`, `start`, the file equals `/academy/courses/33-final-project/files/project.py` (also in the commits) |
| 2 | branch `project/<name>` from start | `git symbolic-ref`, ancestry |
| 3 | project.json complete, frozen | the check's own validation; project.json, project.py, my_metric.py and the listed scenarios unchanged since `before` (commits and working tree) |
| 4 | red test | the test file changed in start..before; at `before` (git archive) pytest of it exits **1** (failures — exit 2 or 4 = could not run is refused); the whole suite: only that file fails |
| 5 | baseline campaign | manifest sha = `before`, project hash, exactly the pre-registered runs, CSV hashes; **one run flown again** by the check from the commit (chosen by a hash of sha + label): byte-identical CSV, or the same metric within 1e-9 (5 % for vision "mine": GPU) |
| 6 | the change | after-sha (from runs/after) descends from `before`; the diff touches the stack (navera_lite/ outside tests, navera_lite.yaml, ref_*.pt); kind stack: `sim/world.py`, `sim/run.py`, `sim/sensors.py` unchanged; kind sim: only `navera_lite/sim/`; the red test file unchanged; test and whole suite pass at the after-sha |
| 7 | after campaign | as 5 for the after-sha; nothing in the stack changed after it (commits or working tree); one run flown again |
| 8 | evaluation.json | the check recomputes every run's metric from the CSVs (its own code), D exactly, the paired CI with its own bootstrap (same algorithm; tolerance 10 % of the width, so an adopted student `stats.py` with another draw order still passes), the guard-rail D, and the decision by the rule |
| 9 | report numbers | sections present with minimum words; before, after, D, CI ends (and the guard-rail's D and CI) correctly rounded with ≥ 2 significant digits (or ×100 for a share), n runs, first/last seed, a changed file named, the test file named + "fail", the metric named |
| 10 | report honesty | section 7's first sentence = the rule's decision (and no other); sections 6–7 say where the interval lies; if not accepted, no unhedged claim (better/improves/fixes/solves… — mission 32's claim rules) in sections 6–8; section 8 mentions simulation and what it lacks |
| 11 | answers.py | PREDICT_* written; EXPLAIN_RED / SEEDS / PAIRED / RULER keyword groups |
| 12 | patch | `my_project.patch` is a git diff containing the changed stack files; `git apply --check -R` passes on the branch |

Badges: **Pre-registered** = checks 1–5; **Measured** = 1–8; **Engineer** = all 12.

Round 1 additions to the table: check 3 also compares the seal; check 4 says when `before` sits on top of the change
(the stack changed between start and before); check 5 recomputes metric and guard-rail on every baseline run and
reports the seal; check 8 follows the metrics' "scenarios", widens 0/1 intervals (Newcombe) and, when an interval
end sits within the tolerance of a decision boundary, accepts evaluate's own decision; check 9 accepts an exact 0
written as 0 (or 0.000); check 10 applies the claim filter (regexes and 21-sentence regression set:
`claims_regression.py`) only to INCONCLUSIVE, or REJECT with D on the bad side, and requires section 8 to name every
after-commit of the journal when there is more than one.

Round 2 additions: the claim filter runs only when D's interval contains 0 (INCONCLUSIVE) or lies on the bad side
(REJECT); when an INCONCLUSIVE interval excludes 0 but crosses the minimum effect (lesson §5 (b)) sections 6–7 must
mention the minimum effect instead; the claim words are wider (earlier, quicker, helps, gain, works, dropped, shorter,
effective, success, should be merged…), a hedge covers only its own clause, and a "case (b)" sentence (minimum effect +
perhaps/less than…) passes — `claims_regression.py`: 43/43 (11 + the reviewer's 18 claims caught, 10 + 4 honest
pass). Check 3 refuses a block that overlaps the seeds in `my_runs/` (exploring). Check 5 marks a seal FIRST stored
when an 'after' campaign or evaluation.json already existed as `…:late` (shown by `tools/seal.py list`). Check 7 sends
`after:<before12>:<after12>` to the server's per-student log (`seals.append`, ≤ 20 values, `stored_log()`); check 10
merges every after-commit from the journal (`campaign after` AND `evaluate` lines), the git refs
`refs/flown/<before12>-<after12>` that `campaign after` writes, runs/after's `afters_history`, evaluation.json and the
server's log, and requires section 8 to name each one when there is more than one. Check 10 also requires section 8 to
name every earlier pre-registration: the commits that wrote project.json in start..before.

**Cannot verify:** whether the change is a good idea, whether the test really pins the problem (beyond "fails
before / passes after"), whether the metric suits the hypothesis, a history rewritten from `start` on purpose (the
earlier pre-registrations are then gone from the branch: `git reflog` in the oral), versions flown and then deleted
(journal, refs/flown and runs/after removed) between two Checks — the server's log only holds what a check saw —,
copying between students (same idea and same seeds: compare repositories). A seal is a FIRST value: a student who
presses Check for the first time after a result gets a `:late` seal (see the rubric). That is the rubric's job
(below). Check time ≈ 1 min 20 s for a complete project (sealed, 60-run plane campaigns).

## Answer key

**Lesson numbers** — all from `make_lesson_numbers.py` (NAVERA_LITE_SIM_DATA=…/datasets/31-simulator, ≈ 30 s):
worked example `lake.json` (GPS jammed 30–75 s, camera blind 45–48 s), seeds 1201–1230, day_timeout_s 5.0 → 2.0,
minimum effect 3 m, guard-rail availability limit 0.02:
err_p95 (fault) before 46.441, after 41.968, D −4.474 m, 95 % CI [−6.046, −3.141] (per-run D from −21.7 to +0.5);
availability 1.000 → 0.951, D −0.049, CI [−0.049, −0.049] (every run loses the same 2.2 s: NO_FIX from ≈ 46.2 s (the last picture, 44.1 s, turns stale) to the
first fix after the blackout, ≈ 48.4 s); err_median D −0.727 [−0.823, −0.625]; err_max D −10.5 [−14.1, −6.8]; first
5 seeds only: err_p95 D −2.34, CI [−3.64, −1.04] (crosses −3 → inconclusive). Per-run sd of err_p95 before 6.47 m,
after 4.24 m; independent campaigns would give √(6.47² + 4.24²) = 7.73 m, the paired differences 4.21 m (r 0.77).
Separate CIs of the mean err_p95: before [44.4, 48.8], after [40.5, 43.5] (the script prints them). The lesson's
0/1 sentence: Wilson upper end of 0/30 = 3.84 / 33.84 = 0.114; below 0.05 needs n > 73.
Idea 1 exploring: jam seed 101, honest2 (fault) 0.725 (≈ "70 %" in the solution report).
Figures: `make_figures.py` (loop, commits, decision: diagrams; paired: the worked example's 30 runs).

**✏️ checks:** §1 nothing can be concluded (two changes); §2 the limit was chosen after the result; §3 exit 2 =
error, not red (import inside the function); §4 1. pairs cancel shared noise, 2. best of N — a second campaign is a
new pre-registration, report both; §5 (a) accept (b) inconclusive (c) inconclusive (d) reject; §6 "contains 0 — not
shown", no "improves".

**Step 0:** PREDICT_SUITE ungraded; the suite: **164 passed** (≈ 13 s); `project.py one campaign/jam.json 101`: honest2 (fault) **0.725** — the stated σ is
too optimistic (0.86 would be honest), the hook of idea 1.

**EXPLAIN rubrics (3 levels; the check only catches empty / off-topic answers):**

| Item | Full | Partial | Insufficient |
|---|---|---|---|
| EXPLAIN_RED | a test that passes on the old code does not see the problem, so it proves nothing about the change; failing first is evidence that it checks the new behaviour (and it stays as a regression test) | "it must fail" without why | "so we know the code is wrong" (about the code, not the test) |
| EXPLAIN_SEEDS | chosen afterwards, one could keep the seeds that favour the change (best of N / forking path); a consecutive block fixed in advance removes that freedom | "to be fair" without the mechanism | "seeds make it reproducible" (true, but not the question) |
| EXPLAIN_PAIRED | the same seeds give the same noise and faults; in the difference the shared part cancels (Var(a − b) with Cov > 0), so only the change remains and the interval is narrower | "to compare the same thing" | "to have more runs" |
| EXPLAIN_RULER | world.py is the measuring instrument; if it changes with the stack, a difference could come from the world, not from the change; a new model goes before 'before' (or is a kind-sim project) | "it must not change" | about the code style |

**Example solution** (idea 1, `_project/`, played by `_apply.sh`): `aged_sigma(σ, age, v) = √(σ² + (v·age)²)` in
`arbiter.py`, used in `Arbiter.step`; setting `age_speed_mps` 15.0 in DEFAULTS and the yaml; the old
`test_step_states_and_switches` pinned the σ of a 0.5 s old GPS fix (3.0 m → would be 8.1 m) and now runs with
`age_speed_mps=0.0` (it tests states and switches) — a real "old test disagrees" case for the lesson's §3; note that
`test_settings` requires the shipped yaml == DEFAULTS, so a default 0.0 with 15.0 in the yaml fails (students meet
it: Step 6 hint 2). Campaign jam + lake, seeds 1001–1020 (40 runs), honest2 closer 0.86, min effect 0.02, guard-rail
fix_share max loss 0.10: before 0.0898, after 0.0582 (means 0.770 → 0.918: from optimistic to too cautious),
D −0.0316, CI [−0.0589, −0.0054] (crosses −0.02); fix_share 1.000 → 0.969, D −0.0311, CI [−0.0404, −0.0218] →
**INCONCLUSIVE** — kept on purpose as the teacher's example: an honest inconclusive report earns full marks. (In the
first build, with seeds 301–320, the same change was ACCEPTED: D −0.111 [−0.140, −0.082] — a good classroom
illustration of why the block of seeds is fixed before the result.) With age speed 30 m/s (the drone's top speed)
honest2 rises to ≈ 0.98 (far too cautious) and fix_share collapses (≈ −0.58 on the old lake): the guard-rail rejects —
a good discussion for idea-1 students. (Exploring numbers of 2026-10-15, `build/exp/e3.py` in the build folder.)

## The project menu — teacher notes per idea (verified in the stack on 2026-10-15)

1. ★ **Ageing σ.** Works as above. Design choices to discuss: which speed (cruise, top, measured from the last two
   GPS fixes), only vision or all sources (GPS ages 0–0.2 s: σ 1.8 → 3.5 m at 15 m/s), DEGRADED threshold effects
   (σ > 25 m → DEGRADED). NAVERA did the equivalent on 2026-10-03 (VALIDATION_STATUS, "carried to the present",
   simulator only).
2. ★★ **Frozen GPS.** Setup in `sim/world.py`: add `"frozen"` to `FAULTS["gps"]` (run.py's `check_scenario` reads
   that tuple) and in `gps_fix` repeat the position of the first frozen fix (no noise, still valid); a scenario with
   `[30, "gps", "frozen"]`. Detector: N identical positions in a row (a real receiver has noise) in the judge's
   `receive` or the guard. Measured by the round-1 reviewer (seeds 301–330, frozen 30–70 s, drone): the existing guard
   already refuses it after `detect_s` 5.4–8.4 s (mean 7.07 s; day vision disagrees `refuse_n` = 5 times), NAVERA
   Lite's error reaching ~90–110 m; a `frozen_n` = 5 rule gives 0.8 s in every run (D −6.27 s [−6.57, −5.97]). The
   effect is deterministic and the simulated noise never repeats a position, so `false_alarm` on the honest part
   cannot show the price (a hover): ask for that limit in the report.
3. ★★★ **Tilted ellipse.** NAVERA fact (verified in base code, read only: its estimator reads σ = √max(a, c) at two
   places; logged as B13 in the problems doc). NAVERA Lite: `estimate.stated_sigma` uses √max(a, c) (taught in 12 and
   27). Setup: a vision profile with an elongated error (e.g. 30 m × 5 m at 45°) drawn and STATED with b ≠ 0 —
   `world.cov_of` is round today, so the setup edits `ProfileVision.locate`/`cov_of`. √max(a, c) = 21.5 m vs the long
   axis 30 m for that example: FIX instead of DEGRADED (limit 25 m) — a visible effect on `fix_share` and `bad_fix`.
4. ★★★ **Night lock-in.** NAVERA fact: mission 25's TEACHER (B16), night gate compares with its own dead-reckoned
   anchor. In NAVERA Lite `night_lag.json` (vision "measured", night, jam at 30 s): the night estimate follows 25 % of
   the motion; seed 5: NAVERA Lite's error 83 m after 5 s, 438 m at 60 s; the autopilot's filter refuses the fixes,
   resets on them after 5 s (59.4 s) and its error jumps to 433 m, 840 m at the end. A detector that refuses the
   lagging source gives NO_FIX → failsafe LAND after 5 s: the guard-rail `failsafe` (0 → 1 in every run) makes the
   trade-off explicit; a good report argues which is safer.
5. ★★★ **Star fix and compass.** NAVERA numbers from VALIDATION_STATUS (end to end 2026-09-30: 5.5/6.5 km perfect,
   53 km tilt 0.5°, 91 km + heading 2°). The simulator has no celestial source: the setup adds one (error ≈ 111.2 km ×
   √(tilt² + (heading_err · cos alt)²), mission 26's rule) fed with a heading from a stack function; the change gives
   it the true heading. Agree the design with the student; the corridor is 1 × 3.8 km, so the metric must be the
   celestial fix's own error or whether the judge uses it, not the flight's arrival.
6. ★★★ **Inliers.** NAVERA fact: validation report says ≥ 6 inliers (2026-10-03); the product module's default is 8
   (verified in base code, read only; B12). NAVERA Lite: `match.gates(min_inliers=6)` and `locate.DEFAULTS` — the
   simulator's day pipeline (`sim/vision.py`, vision "mine") calls `gates` with its default. A day "mine" run takes
   ≈ 45 s for 100 s of flight on the Jetson (the map's descriptors are cached after the first run): keep scenarios
   ≈ 40 s and 20 runs (≈ 7 min per campaign). Changing `sim/vision.py` is allowed for kind stack (only world, run and
   sensors are the ruler).
7. ★ **Guard's patience.** `spoof.GUARD_DEFAULTS` (n disagreeing fixes, p_fa). Metric `detect_s` with
   `"scenarios": ["campaign/drift.json"]`; guard-rail `false_alarm` with `"scenarios": ["campaign/plane_late.json",
   "campaign/baseline.json"]` (mission 31's R9 already fails on plane_late: the guard refuses the honest GPS). A 0/1
   guard-rail needs 60–80 runs per scenario to show a rate below 0.05 (runs take 0.2–0.5 s).
8. ★★ **Late camera.** Mission 31's diagnosis: pictures 1.5 s old stamped "now" on a 40 m/s plane → 60 m that the
   guard's time-gap term does not cover. Three designs measured by the round-2 reviewer on exploring seeds:

   | Design | false alarm (late camera) | drift detection |
   |---|---|---|
   | A. latency in the gap term: g = max_speed × (\|Δt\| + 1.5 s) | 0 | **detected 0 in 5/5**: a 150 m gap term (100 m/s × 1.5 s) blinds the χ² test |
   | B. shift every camera fix by 1.5 s | 0 when late from 0 s; still 1 on `plane_late` (on time for its first 20 s) | on-time camera: the GPS is refused at once |
   | C. test the fix at its stamp AND at stamp − 1.5 s, keep the better match | 0 on both | late camera 12–19 → 47–51 s; on-time 18–23 → 22–26 s |

   Metric `false_alarm` on a late-camera plane scenario (`"scenarios"`), Newcombe interval; guard-rail **`detect_s`**
   on a plane drift scenario with the same camera (`"scenarios"`) — `detected` alone stays 1 → 1 while detection is
   30 s later. (Round-2 reviewer, seeds 2001–2030: design C false_alarm 30/30 → 0/30, D −1.000 [−1.000, −0.8395];
   detect_s 19.47 → 48.70 s, D +29.2 [27.3, 31.1] → REJECT at a 10 s limit.) Ask for the bias in the Limits: the old
   guard's quick "detection" on a late camera is helped by its own false alarms.
9. ★★★ **Retrain the night network.** `homography_net.make_pairs` on `/data/academy/25-thermal-night/scenes_train.npz`,
   `train` through `academy_gpu` (≤ 5 min GPU); the change is `ref_homography.pt` (commit the training script too).
   NEVER train on the corridor (`/data/academy/31-simulator/corridor/night_*.png`): the campaign would measure memory.
   `night_mine` ≈ 6.5 s per run (GPU, not bit-exact: the check's re-flight uses a 5 % tolerance on the metric).
10. ★★ **GPS bursts (kind sim).** `sim/sensors.py` / `world.gps_fix`: rare bursts of tens of metres for a few seconds.
    The stack must not change (the check enforces it). The report's conclusion is about the model ("under bursts the
    stack's err_p95 rises by …"); remind them that "accept" means "the hypothesised effect is shown".

## Rubric for the project (the open part, 20 points)

| Criterion | 4 — excellent | 2 — adequate | 0 — insufficient |
|---|---|---|---|
| Problem | a real NAVERA Lite problem, shown in an exploring run with a number; linked to the NAVERA problem in words when there is one | plausible but not shown | no problem, or a cosmetic change |
| Pre-registration | metric and window measure the hypothesis; minimum effect and guard-rail limit justified by the use (not by the data); enough runs | sensible but unjustified numbers | metric unrelated to the hypothesis, or no guard-rail where the change has an obvious price |
| Test and change | red test pins the new behaviour on hand-made inputs (boundary + old behaviour kept); one concern per commit; old tests handled honestly (§3); clean design | test passes/fails correctly but is thin | test asserts the implementation, or an old test deleted/weakened without reason |
| Measurement and decision | scenarios exercise the problem; decision quoted with the interval; zero-width or surprising intervals explained | correct but unexplained | numbers without the interval, or a decision against the rule |
| Report honesty | every claim matches the interval; limits concrete (what the simulator lacks, what to fly next); a field plan | generic limits | claims beyond the data; "simulation" hidden |

Levels 3 and 1 lie between the descriptions. **The decision is never graded**: an honest REJECT or INCONCLUSIVE can
earn 20/20; an ACCEPT reached by a metric or limit that does not match the hypothesis loses the Pre-registration
points. Difficulty: a ★★★ project that ends inconclusive with an excellent report is worth as much as a ★ project that
is accepted; do not add stars to the score. A setup (new fault or model) committed with the red test and tested itself
counts under "Test and change: 4". **Oral (5 min, Session 3):** the student shows `git log --oneline --decorate
--graph`, `runs/journal.txt`, explains one interval and answers "what would make you change your decision?" — use it to
confirm the criteria above, not as a sixth one. **Integrity:** a pre-registration changed after the badge without a
reset (the seal fails), or several "after" versions evaluated and not reported (journal), sets Pre-registration and
Report honesty to 0. A second pre-registration made with your reset is
not penalised when section 8 names both and says why; a seal marked `:late` (`tools/seal.py list`) means the rule was
frozen after a result existed: Pre-registration at most 2/4 unless the reflog shows otherwise. **Final mark:** checks 40 % (badges Pre-registered 10 %, Measured 15 %, Engineer 15 % — or as your
department uses), rubric 60 %.

## Difficulties seen in testing

- (round 1 reviewer) following the old menu literally (metric on one scenario, guard-rail on another) made
  `evaluate` die after both campaigns; now the menu uses `"scenarios"` and `campaign before` refuses an undefined
  metric at once. Re-tagging `before` on top of the change: `red` and check 4 now say so, and lab Step 5 hint 2 /
  Step 8 hint 1 give the `git switch -c … before` + `cherry-pick` commands.
- pytest exit code 2 or 4 (an import of a not-yet-existing name at the top of the test file: 4 for the file alone, 2 for the suite): `red` and the check refuse
  it; lesson §3 and Step 4 hint 2.
- A new setting only in the yaml (default 0.0): `test_settings` fails (yaml must equal DEFAULTS). Step 6 hint 2.
- An old test pins the old behaviour (idea 1: `test_step_states_and_switches`). Step 6 hint 1; never delete.
- `campaign after` refuses a dirty stack; `green` warns that uncommitted changes are not tested.
- A metric undefined in some run (no row in its window, e.g. an error metric when the run ends before the fault):
  `evaluate` refuses; it needs a new pre-registration.
- Students who try `git tag before` twice get "already exists": `git tag -f before` only BEFORE Step 6.

## Class plan (3 sessions)

- **Session 1 (1 h 30 – 3 h):** 15 min lesson §1–§2 together (the forking paths with the worked example's 0.02 vs
  0.05 limit); Step 0–1 alone; ideas presented in 10 min; each student explores and pre-registers; the teacher
  reviews each project.json before the tag (2 min per student: is the metric the hypothesis?). Badge Pre-registered.
- **Session 2 (2 h – 3 h):** the change, green, the after campaign, evaluate. Ask for a prediction before the
  evaluation (PREDICT_EFFECT). Badge Measured.
- **Session 3 (1 h – 1 h 30):** report and patch; a 5-minute oral per student or team: show the branch (`git log
  --oneline --decorate`), the reflog, the figure, defend the decision.
- **Differentiation.** Struggling: idea 1 (fully hinted) or 7 (a settings change with a clear trade-off), 20 runs,
  one scenario. Fast: a ★★★ idea, a second pre-registration on the plane (Going further), a mutant of their own fix.
  Teams on the same idea pre-register different seed blocks and compare intervals.
